adultGuide.title: Spiral Notebook Story Final Copy Adult Guide
bullets: Print the spiral notebook final copy cards, take-home slips, and adult guide pages before the adult-led paper session.
Start with one fictional revised draft, then guide the writer through title, first line, paragraph spacing, careful copying, gentle rereading, and final note work.
Keep every example invented, family-friendly, offline, paper-only, and guided by an adult.
Use the spiral notebook page as the clean copy space, with pencil marks kept light and easy to follow.
Keep all names, places, and objects inside the pretend story world so no private details are needed.
Finish by having the writer choose one proud sentence and one next-story note on paper.

finalCopyRoutines.name: Title Line Setup
finalCopyRoutines.bestFor: Helping the final copy begin with a clear title line on the spiral notebook page.
steps: The adult asks which pretend story title belongs at the top of the spiral notebook page: ____________________.
The writer points to the title on the revised draft before copying it: ____________________.
The adult asks where the title should sit so the story page feels easy to read: ____________________.
The writer copies the title neatly on the first clean line: ____________________.

finalCopyRoutines.name: First Line Start
finalCopyRoutines.bestFor: Starting the final copy with a first sentence that matches the revised draft.
steps: The adult asks the writer to find the first sentence in the revised fictional draft: ____________________.
The writer places a finger under the first words that will be copied: ____________________.
The adult asks what the first sentence should help the reader know right away: ____________________.
The writer copies the first sentence on the clean spiral notebook page: ____________________.

finalCopyRoutines.name: Paragraph Space Check
finalCopyRoutines.bestFor: Leaving enough space between story parts so the final copy is easy to follow.
steps: The adult marks where the first story part ends on the revised draft: ____________________.
The writer decides where a small space or new line should go on the notebook page: ____________________.
The adult asks which next story part should begin after the space: ____________________.
The writer copies the next part with clear spacing: ____________________.

finalCopyRoutines.name: Copy One Chunk
finalCopyRoutines.bestFor: Copying a short piece at a steady paper pace without rushing the page.
steps: The adult chooses one short chunk from the revised draft for the writer to copy: ____________________.
The writer reads the chunk once with a finger under the words: ____________________.
The adult asks which words the writer will copy before looking back at the draft: ____________________.
The writer copies that chunk onto the spiral notebook page: ____________________.

finalCopyRoutines.name: Gentle Reread Pass
finalCopyRoutines.bestFor: Checking the copied page against the revised draft with calm adult support.
steps: The adult reads one copied sentence while the writer follows the revised draft: ____________________.
The writer marks any missing or doubled word with a tiny pencil dot: ____________________.
The adult asks what the sentence should say after the small fix: ____________________.
The writer makes one quiet correction on the final copy page: ____________________.

finalCopyRoutines.name: Proud Sentence Note
finalCopyRoutines.bestFor: Ending the final copy pass with a positive paper note and one next-story idea.
steps: The adult asks the writer to choose one copied sentence that feels clear and strong: ____________________.
The writer underlines that sentence lightly on the spiral notebook page: ____________________.
The adult asks what the writer wants to remember for the next fictional story: ____________________.
The writer adds one next-story note at the bottom of the page: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Title Copy Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Copy the pretend story title on the first clean line of the spiral notebook page: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask where the title should sit so the page is easy to read: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: First Sentence Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Find the first sentence in the revised draft, then copy it onto the clean page: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask what the first sentence helps the reader know: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Chunk Copy Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Copy one short story chunk from the revised draft onto the spiral notebook page: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask which words the writer will copy before looking back: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Spacing Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Leave a clear space or new line where the next story part begins: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask which story part should begin after the space: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Margin Dot Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Put a tiny pencil dot beside one place to revisit on the copied page: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask what that sentence should say after the small fix: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Missing Word Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Compare one copied line with the revised draft and add any missing word: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask which draft word belongs in the copied line: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Doubled Word Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Find one doubled word on the copied page and cross out only the extra word: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask how the sentence reads after the extra word comes out: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Clear Ending Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Copy the final sentence from the revised draft onto the notebook page: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask how the ending lets the reader know the story is finished: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Proud Sentence Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Lightly underline one copied sentence that feels clear and strong: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask why that sentence is a good one to keep: ____________________.

takeHomeFinalCopySlips.title: Next Story Note Slip
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.direction: Write one note at the bottom of the page for the next fictional story: ____________________.
takeHomeFinalCopySlips.familyLine: Ask what the writer wants to remember next time: ____________________.
